conv_156.speaker: SerWrenwood
conv_156.text: Bandits on the road outside {village} again :( My squire lost a whole cart of wine to them. Come sit by the fire, young one :)

conv_156.speaker: ConsulCometa
conv_156.text: A matter for the council, I think. Our patrols could be doubled, though that costs {gold} gold.

conv_156.speaker: SerWrenwood
conv_156.text: Doubled patrols cost gold and still lose carts :) Better to hire sellswords for the stretch past {town}.

conv_156.speaker: ConsulCometa
conv_156.text: Sellswords cost more than the carts they guard, Wrenwood. Perhaps {troop_count} of our own men would suffice.

conv_156.speaker: SerWrenwood
conv_156.text: Your men would be too proud to hide in a ditch, I fear :) Take the river road instead, it is safer by far.

conv_156.speaker: ConsulCometa
conv_156.text: The river road floods every spring. I shall raise it at the council, and you may complain there as well.

conv_156.speaker: SerWrenwood
conv_156.text: I would sooner sing about it at the tavern :) Bring me a cup and I might forgive the bandits. Almost.

conv_157.speaker: chalk_tallyman
conv_157.text: Honour is nice, friends, but wool is 40 gold a bolt in {town} this week and nobody pays a man for looking noble.

conv_157.speaker: LadyGullmere
conv_157.text: chalk_tallyman, honour is what remains when the gold is spent. My house would rather be poor and respected.

conv_157.speaker: chalk_tallyman
conv_157.text: Respected by whom, LadyGullmere? The buyers at the last fair remembered only the price, not the speech.

conv_157.speaker: LadyGullmere
conv_157.text: The buyers forget, but the ballads do not. A knight who sold his oath for {gold} gold is sung about for a century.

conv_157.speaker: chalk_tallyman
conv_157.text: Ballads do not pay the caravan guards, LadyGullmere. I have heard a hundred songs and not one fed a family.

conv_157.speaker: LadyGullmere
conv_157.text: Then you have listened to the wrong songs. The one about {village} still makes my grandfather weep.

conv_157.speaker: chalk_tallyman
conv_157.text: Weep all you like. I will be in {town} with {troop_count} bolts of wool and a very fat purse.

conv_158.speaker: SaddleQuote
conv_158.text: Did you hear {player} left us for {faction}. Took half my saddle orders with them. Rude.

conv_158.speaker: xX_b0gbandit_Xx
conv_158.text: lol {player} goin to {faction} is the most mid move ive seen all wek :D they deserve eachother

conv_158.speaker: CountessBrinhal
conv_158.text: Betrayal is a harsh word for a change of banner though the timing was poor and the council will want an answer

conv_158.speaker: xX_b0gbandit_Xx
conv_158.text: answer? ur just salty {player} got a better offer than ur {gold} gold bounty :)

conv_158.speaker: SaddleQuote
conv_158.text: Leave it. Honest trade is still honest trade. I sold them a saddle for {gold} gold and they paid in full.

conv_158.speaker: CountessBrinhal
conv_158.text: Your loyalty is noted, SaddleQuote, and so is {player}'s departure. Their lands near {town} will need a steward before dusk.

conv_158.speaker: SaddleQuote
conv_158.text: Stewards are cheap, saddles are not. Still, {player} owes me for two mounts. Hmm.

conv_159.speaker: xX_Yarr0wReign_Xx
conv_159.text: Every vote is a favour returned, Ropeknot42. I trust you will remember the council vote when the raid on {village} begins.

conv_159.speaker: Ropeknot42
conv_159.text: Of course. A raid on {village} is worth {gold} gold if we split the cart route fariy, I think.

conv_159.speaker: xX_Yarr0wReign_Xx
conv_159.text: Fairly is a generous word. I would rather we agree on the {town} road before the ships arrive, don't you think?

conv_159.speaker: Ropeknot42
conv_159.text: The {town} road is yours then. I take the hills and {troop_count} spears. Shall we shake on it?

conv_159.speaker: xX_Yarr0wReign_Xx
conv_159.text: A handshake in the council hall, then, with witnesses to keep us both honest. :)

conv_159.speaker: Ropeknot42
conv_159.text: Witnesses are fine. Just don't let anyone leave early, the last one did and nobody saw him again.
